Reading a file without reading a file

By Mira Halvorsen on 4 March 2026

Our importer spent most of its wall clock in one place, and it was not where anyone expected. The parser was fine. The read_to_string in front of it was not.

What the profile said

The shape of the problem is easier to see as a list, so here it is as one, with the detail underneath each point:

  1. Every ledger file was read whole into memory.
    • Even the ones we skipped after the first line.
    • Even the ones that had not changed since the last run.
  2. The allocator saw one enormous request per file.
  3. Then the parser copied it again, into its own arena.

The fix was to stop reading the file:

let file = File::open(path)?;
let mapped = unsafe { Mmap::map(&file)? };

for line in mapped.split(|byte| *byte == b'\n') {
    if !line.starts_with(b"2026-") {
        continue;
    }
    entries.push(Entry::parse(line)?);
}

A memory map is not free, and it is not always right. On a network filesystem it is worse than the read it replaces. But our files are local and large, and the numbers moved:

Nine hundred milliseconds became forty. We did not make the parser faster. We stopped handing it work it had not asked for.

The bit that bit us

Mmap is unsafe for a reason: another process truncating the file underneath you is undefined behaviour, not an error you can catch. We took a lock. 

$ cargo bench --bench import
import/small     time:   [39.211 ms 39.884 ms 40.702 ms]
import/large     time:   [412.09 ms 418.77 ms 426.31 ms]

The full patch is here, and the benchmark harness is in the same folder.
